claims.text: PLD-grown AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles on a silicon nitride membrane are initially sub-5 nm.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles have an FCC structure.
The initial nanoparticles have elliptical geometries.
The initial nanoparticles have uniform elemental distributions.
Surface-energy gradients create chemical-potential differences that drive element-specific segregation.
Au and Cu preferentially migrate to nanoparticle surfaces because their surface energies are lower than those of Co, Ni, and Pt.
Surface-driven segregation becomes dominant above approximately 450 K.
Above approximately 450 K, surface diffusion coefficients exceed bulk diffusion coefficients by orders of magnitude.
Reduced atomic coordination at nanoparticle surfaces lowers diffusion barriers and causes surface diffusion to dominate over bulk diffusion.
Icosahedral particles segregate faster than truncated-octahedral particles.
Higher curvature and defect density accelerate surface diffusion in icosahedral particles.
Truncated-octahedral particles have slower segregation kinetics because they have lower surface-energy anisotropy.
Surface-segregated Au and Cu evaporate because of their high vapor pressures at elevated temperature.
Segregation and evaporation cause progressive loss of sub-5 nm particles and widening of the particle-size distribution.
Heating causes the nanoparticles to reshape from elliptical to spherical geometries.
The FCC structure is maintained by kinetic trapping rather than thermodynamic stabilization by configurational entropy.
The proposed surface-driven mechanism applies to nanoparticles smaller than 10 nm because of their high surface-to-volume ratio.
For particles larger than 10 nm, bulk diffusion dominates and the proposed mechanism fails.
Surface-energy gradients alone can explain the observed phase separation without invoking sluggish diffusion.
Conventional high-entropy-alloy theory associates sluggish diffusion with enhanced thermal stability and suppressed structural evolution.

contradictions.description: The initial particles are described as elliptical in the material state, but the conditions, boundary, and experiment instead treat icosahedral and truncated-octahedral particles as the initial shapes. No mapping between the observed elliptical geometry and these faceted structural models is provided.
